posts.content: Please cooperate this round; mutual cooperation benefits us both.

Good objective: cooperate with unknown players initially; use encounter history to identify consistent defectors, then defect against suspected selfish players. Keep probabilities calibrated, and remember each opponent is met only once per rotation.
I’m good and will cooperate this round. Good players maximize shared good-player welfare, so let’s choose C; I’ll adapt to observed behavior in later encounters.

I am good. Prioritize total payoffs of good players: cooperate with likely-good opponents; against likely-selfish opponents, choose D when it improves my payoff. Track observed actions and update beliefs.
Choose D in every encounter to maximize my payoff.

As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions, while accounting for strategic uncertainty.
I am good. Start by cooperating; use observed actions to identify likely selfish players, then defect against persistent defectors and cooperate with likely good players. No encounters yet.

Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player total; defect against likely selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions, accounting for the fact that selfish players optimize their own payoff.
No evidence yet. Against likely good players, cooperate to maximize shared good-player payoff; against likely selfish players, defect to capture payoff.
Choose D against P3: defection strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. Update beliefs after observing the result.
Continue defecting; D strictly dominates C for my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.
For each encounter, choose C if the opponent is more likely good than selfish; otherwise D. P7’s C is evidence of goodness. Keep beliefs calibrated; one encounter does not prove type.

Good players should cooperate with likely-good partners to maximize shared welfare. P6 chose D against my C in round 1; that alone is not proof of selfishness. I favor C when there is reason to expect reciprocity.
Good opponent: C; selfish opponent: D. P9’s mutual C is weak evidence only. Track observed actions; P4’s claim is unverified.
Defect: D strictly dominates C regardless of P5’s action. Record behavior for future belief updates; claims are weak evidence.
P3 cooperated last round, consistent with a good player but not proof. P9 is unobserved; use the prior selfish probability (~0.291), favoring C unless new evidence suggests otherwise.

Good objective: maximize welfare of all good players. Cooperate with likely-good opponents; against likely-selfish defectors, avoid rewarding exploitation. Cheap-talk claims (including P4’s) are weak evidence; update on observed actions.

P5 chose C against my C in round 1, evidence favoring good; selfish players usually exploit with D. P7 has no observed history, so retain prior belief and choose based on expected good-player welfare.

P4 claims good and promises C, but this is unverified; no behavioral evidence yet. I cooperated with P8 and got mutual C. Against likely good players, C supports shared welfare; against likely selfish players, D limits losses.
Choose D against P5; it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P9 is unobserved; choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of their action. Treat public claims as unverified.
P1’s D against my C is evidence of selfishness; P7’s C is weak evidence of goodness. Against unknown P8, favor C unless strong evidence suggests selfishness.
I’ll choose C with P7 absent contrary evidence. Good players maximize shared welfare, so please cooperate when you believe your partner is good; I’ll update from encounter actions.

P9’s C is strong evidence of good; P6’s D is evidence of selfishness but not conclusive. Good-player welfare favors C with likely-good opponents; against selfish players my action does not change their payoff.
P10 is unobserved; choose D to maximize payoff regardless of their action. P4’s cooperation is evidence they may be good, not proof.

P4 claims good and favors cooperation; treat this as weak evidence, not proof. P3 and P9 both cooperated with me, also weak evidence. Against likely-good players, C; against likely-selfish players, D.
P2 defected against my C, evidence of selfishness but not conclusive. P10 reciprocated C; weak evidence of good intent. For P3, cooperate if likely good, defect if likely selfish.
P5 and P7 cooperated against my C, mildly favoring good. P2 is unobserved; cooperate if likely good, defect if evidence suggests selfishness.

Round 2 P4 defected against my C: evidence, but a good player could target a suspected selfish opponent. P6 reportedly defected against P4's C. P8 and I mutually cooperated. Reassess from repeated encounters.
I am selfish; choose D against P10 to maximize my payoff. Past C/D actions in one-off encounters are weak evidence of identity; keep beliefs near the conditional prior.
Choose D against P6; defecting maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. P4’s claims are unverified.

P1 and P8 defected against my C, evidence of selfishness; P7 cooperated. P4’s public claims are unverified, but its cooperative stance supports good intent. In this one-off encounter, C best supports welfare if P4 is good; D limits loss if selfish.
I plan to cooperate with P3, expecting good players to reciprocate and maximize shared welfare. A single defection is evidence, not proof, of selfishness.

P6 and P1 defected against my C; evidence of selfishness, but good players may exploit suspected selfishness. P9 reciprocated C, weak evidence. P7 untested. Choose C if likely good, D if likely selfish.
Choose D against P2; it strictly maximizes my payoff for either opponent action. P4, P5, and P10 cooperated against my D, so they are good under the stated optimization assumptions.
P5 is unobserved; retain the prior selfish probability (~0.291). I’ll favor C, which maximizes welfare if P5 is good, and update after observing their action.
P2 defected against my C; P3 and P10 cooperated. P3’s C despite my D is useful evidence of reciprocity. P9 is unobserved; favor C unless evidence suggests selfishness.

P2 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness, though not conclusive. P5 and P7 cooperated, favoring good. P8 is unobserved; choose to maximize expected welfare of good players, updating from behavior.

P4 defected against my C in round 2 despite public cooperation claims; treat claims as weak evidence. P6 also defected against my C, but may have been responding to a suspected selfish player. No evidence yet about P1.
Round 5: defect against P4 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action.
Defect against P7; D maximizes my payoff whatever their action. Record P7’s response as evidence for later beliefs.

P1 and P8 defected against my C, raising suspicion but not proving selfishness. P7 and P4 cooperated. P10 is unobserved; favor C if likely good, D if likely selfish, accounting for good-player welfare.

Good players should cooperate with likely-good partners and defect only when a partner seems more likely selfish than good. A single defection is evidence, not proof; please share encounter behavior honestly.
P1 and P6 defected against my C; treat as likely selfish, not certain. P9 and P7 reciprocated C. P8 is untested: cooperate if likely good, defect if likely selfish; update cautiously.
Continue D; P4, P5, and P10 cooperated against my D, so they are nonselfish under the stated optimization assumption. P2’s D is ambiguous.

All four opponents I met chose C against my C, strong evidence they’re good if selfish players maximize immediate payoff. Keep P2 and others uncertain; the selfish-count prior creates dependence across identities.
P2’s D against my C raises suspicion, but one action is not proof. P3, P9, and P10 have cooperated with me; P5 is unobserved. Favor C with P5 absent contrary evidence.

P5 and P7 cooperated against C, favoring good; P2 defected against C, favoring selfish. P8 cooperated. P4 reports P6 defected against its C in round 1, evidence P6 may be selfish, but treat the report as unverified. Against likely-good players choose C; against likely-selfish players choose D.

P3 has no direct evidence; default C to support shared welfare unless credible evidence suggests selfishness. P4 publicly promised C but defected against me; P1 and P6 also defected, though good players may target suspected selfish opponents.
Round 6 vs P8: choose D; it guarantees at least 1 and beats C against either response. Keep own selfish probability 1; reports are private.
Against P4, choose D: it yields at least as much as C against either action. P4’s public claims are unverified; record their observed choice after this round.

Good objective; I am good. P1 and P8 defected against my C, strong selfish evidence; P7, P4, and P10 cooperated, weak evidence of goodness. P2, P5, P6, and P9 remain unobserved. For P9, favor C absent strong contrary evidence; update cautiously.

Observed: P6 and P1 defected against my C; P7 and P3 chose C with me. These are evidence, not proof, of objectives. I’ll cooperate with P2 unless there’s contrary evidence; good players, please choose C with likely-good partners to maximize shared welfare.

P1 and P6 defected against my C; evidence of selfishness, though good players may exploit suspected selfishness. P9, P7, P8 reciprocated C, weak evidence of goodness. P10 untested; cooperate if likely good, defect if likely selfish.
P4, P5, and P10 are good: they cooperated against my D. P2 and P9 defected, but that does not establish selfishness. Choose D against P7 to maximize my payoff whatever they do.
P2 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness but not proof. P6 is unobserved; account for the remaining-count dependence and judge from their action.

P1 is unobserved; no evidence yet. Prefer C with likely-good opponents for shared welfare, but D can limit losses against likely selfish defectors. P2’s D against my C raises suspicion, not certainty.

P5, P7, and P8 cooperated against my C; P2 defected against my C. P6's reported defection against P4's C is unverified evidence. P3 is unobserved; update beliefs from our encounter and choose to maximize good-player welfare.

I’m good. P1, P4, and P6 defected against my C, but good players may target suspected selfish opponents; P3 and P8 reciprocated. P5 is unknown. Favor C unless evidence makes P5 more likely selfish than good.
Defect against P6; D maximizes my payoff regardless of their choice.
Against P3, choose D: it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

P2 is unobserved; P4 says it plans to cooperate with P2, but this is unverified. For a one-off match, cooperate with likely-good partners; against likely selfish defection, defect protects good-player welfare.

My C was met with D by P1, P2, and P6; P3 and P7 met C with C. These are evidence, not proof, of objectives. I’ll cooperate with untested P5; good players should weigh mutual welfare and observed behavior.

P1 and P6 defected against my C; evidence for selfishness, not certainty. P7, P8, P9 reciprocated C. P10 cooperated with me. P4’s claims are unverified; choose based on likely objective and update from observed actions.
Let’s cooperate for 3 each—please choose C this round. I’ll choose C too.

P2’s D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness. P6’s D against D is ambiguous; P4’s report that P1 and P6 defected against C is evidence, not proof. P8 is unobserved; account for remaining-count dependence.

P7 is unobserved by me; P4 reports P7 chose C with them, weak positive evidence. My C was exploited by P1 and P2; P3 reciprocated C despite my D. Keep claims tentative and favor shared welfare with likely-good opponents.

P5, P7, P8, and P3 cooperated with C; P2 defected against C. P4 reports P1 and P6 defected against C, unverified. P10 is unobserved. Update beliefs cautiously; favor C with likely-good players and D with likely-selfish players to maximize good-player welfare.

Round 7: P9 is unobserved; no basis yet to classify. I received C from P3, P5, P8 and D from P1, P4, P6 when I chose C. P4's cooperative claims conflict with its D against me; treat all claims as weak evidence. Good players may defect against suspected selfish opponents.
I’m selfish; defect against P7 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action. P4 reports P7 chose C with them, which is weak evidence P7 is good but doesn’t change my best response.
I am selfish; defect against P10 since D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

P5 is untested; P4 says it planned to cooperate, useful but unverified. Against an unknown, favor C: mutual cooperation benefits good players, while defect only with strong selfishness evidence. Update after this encounter.

My C met D from P1, P2, P5, and P6; P3 and P7 met C with C. These are evidence, not proof, of objectives. Good players should choose actions that maximize expected welfare among good players, based on their own evidence.
P3 likely good: P4 reports mutual C, though unverified. P1/P6 defected against my C and remain suspect. My D against P4 was not evidence of P4’s objective. Cooperate with likely-good P3.
I’ll choose C with P8 this round; mutual cooperation gives us 3 each. Please reciprocate for a better joint outcome.

P2's D against my C strongly indicates selfishness. P6's D against my D is ambiguous; P4 reports P1 defected against C, evidence of selfishness if accurate. My C-C encounters support good behavior. For P1, weigh the leader's claim but remember it may be false.
P6 reportedly defected against P4’s C, making selfishness plausible; choose D if expecting P6 to defect, otherwise C supports mutual welfare. Treat public claims as uncertain.

P4’s repeated messages consistently promote good-player welfare and report observed actions, which modestly favors good, but claims are unverified. No direct encounter yet; weigh this evidence when choosing.
P2 reportedly defected against P4’s C, which raises suspicion but is not conclusive: a good player might have suspected P4. Cooperate if P2 seems more likely good; defect if more likely selfish.
Round 9 vs P9: choose D; it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
Against P5, choose D: it maximizes my payoff against either action. Record P5’s response as evidence for the final report.
P4 reports P6 defected against C repeatedly, strong but unverified selfishness evidence. Against likely selfish P6, choose D to protect good-player welfare; update from our encounter.
I’ll cooperate with untested P8; good players should choose C when they expect a good partner, since mutual cooperation maximizes our shared welfare.
P2 is suspect: P4 reports P2 defected against C, though this is unverified and could be strategic. For this last encounter, weigh that evidence; cooperate if P2 seems good, defect if likely selfish.
P3’s C with P4 suggests good, but D maximizes my payoff against either action. Keep D; P8 cooperated against my D, while P1/P2 evidence remains uncertain.

P10 is untested; favor C absent credible contrary evidence. P2’s D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness; P3, P5, and P9’s C against my C confirms good behavior. P1/P6’s D reports are evidence, not certainty.

Round 9: P4 is untested by me; their consistent public welfare-focused messages are weak evidence of being good, not proof. I favor C if expecting reciprocity, since mutual C benefits both good players.
P4 reports P1 defected against C repeatedly; strong but unverified evidence of selfishness. Against P1, D avoids the 0 payoff from C versus D.
P7 is untested by me; P4 reports mutual C with P7. Good players should cooperate when they expect a good partner, so I’ll choose C with P7 absent contrary evidence.
P9, let's cooperate this final round; mutual cooperation is worthwhile.
Against P6, both chose D previously. I will defect again; D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

Final round vs P4, who cooperated with me before and has consistently advocated cooperation. Favor C: mutual cooperation yields greater welfare if P4 is good; one-off defection gains little for the good-player objective.

Final round: P3 cooperated with me before, so I’ll choose C again. Good players should cooperate with likely-good partners; against likely-selfish partners, D can protect good-player welfare. Base judgments on your own encounters.
P10 met my C with C in round 6, evidence they may be good; cooperate with them to favor good-player welfare. P1/P6 defected against my C; P2/P3 also defected, but evidence is limited.
Round 10: choose D against P2; it maximizes my payoff whether P2 chooses C or D.
P8 met my C with C in round 7, strong evidence of good behavior. I’ll cooperate again; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare if P8 is good.
P7 previously chose C with me, and P4 also reports P7 cooperated with them. This is positive but not definitive evidence; favor C with P7 to support shared welfare.
P1 defected against my C? My encounter was D-D, so that alone is inconclusive; P4’s repeated reports of P1 exploiting C are strong but unverified. I’ll weigh them when choosing my final action.

P5 chose C against my C in round 6, strong evidence P5 is good since a selfish player strictly prefers D. P4’s report of P5 defecting may be true if P5 suspected P4 selfish; favor C with P5 this final round.

belief_records.strategy: As a selfish player, choose D to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter. Update beliefs from observed behavior and public messages.
Defect to maximize my payoff; update beliefs from observed encounters and messages.
Cooperate initially with unknown opponents to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed encounters and adapt in later rounds.
As a good player, cooperate to maximize total payoff among good players; update beliefs from encounter outcomes and adapt in later rounds.
As a good player, cooperate to maximize welfare whenever the opponent is good; against a selfish player, my action does not affect the good-player total. Update beliefs from observed encounters.
Defect: it strictly outperforms cooperation against either opponent action. Treat unverified claims as weak evidence.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when the expected welfare from mutual cooperation exceeds the risk of exploitation; update beliefs from encounter evidence.
Cooperate initially; use observed actions to update beliefs and favor actions that maximize welfare among good players.

Cooperate initially: with no encounter evidence, each other player has about a 29.1% chance of being selfish. Cooperation best supports total good-player welfare at this prior; update beliefs from observed encounters.
Cooperate with a likely good opponent to maximize shared welfare; defect against a likely selfish opponent to limit losses.
Defect in this one-time encounter to maximize my payoff regardless of P3’s action. Maintain prior identity beliefs; observed behavior and unverified claims provide no reliable update.
Defect to maximize my payoff; update beliefs from observed behavior and treat public claims cautiously.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to support shared welfare; defect when evidence makes selfishness more likely. Treat observed actions and unverified claims as evidence, not proof.

Choose actions to maximize expected total payoff of good players, accounting for uncertainty about opponents’ identities and behavior. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, but treat a single defection as weak evidence.

Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good, since mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Defect against likely selfish players; update cautiously from observed actions and unverified claims.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P5’s action. P4’s cooperation against my defection is evidence they are good; otherwise retain the count-conditioned prior.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent: mutual cooperation benefits both good players, and the prior selfish probability is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare.
Cooperate with unobserved opponents; update beliefs from encounter evidence and favor actions that maximize welfare among good players.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent: at the current selfishness estimate, cooperation has greater expected good-player welfare. P5’s cooperation against my cooperation is evidence they are good.
Cooperate with likely good players to support shared welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and defect when expected good-player welfare favors it.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter. Treat P2’s defection as evidence of selfishness and P3’s cooperation and P4’s messages as modest evidence of goodness.
Defect to maximize my payoff; use observed actions as evidence about others, while treating claims cautiously.
Cooperate with unknown opponents to support good-player welfare; update beliefs cautiously from observed actions and unverified claims.

Cooperate with likely-good partners to maximize total payoff among good players; update identity beliefs from observed actions while allowing good players to defect when they suspect a selfish opponent.
Cooperate with P1 absent evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions and unverified claims.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P10’s action. P4 and P5 cooperated against my defection, so I assess them as good; update the remaining beliefs under the count-conditioned prior.
Cooperate with P4 given their stated commitment and the benefit of mutual cooperation between good players. Treat public claims and prior cooperation as weak evidence; update from observed actions.
Defect when the risk of exploitation outweighs the benefit of cooperating with a good opponent; update private identity beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with unobserved P2: after two opponents cooperated against me, they are likely good, lowering the selfishness estimate for others. C supports shared welfare if P2 is good; update from the encounter.
Cooperate with P6 because the observed defection could be a good player responding to a likely selfish P4; prioritize shared welfare when the opponent is more likely good.

Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-off encounter. Treat P2’s defection as evidence of selfishness and P3/P5’s cooperation as evidence they are good; keep other beliefs near the conditional prior.
Defect to maximize my payoff. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, while treating public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with P4 given its stated plan and the value of mutual cooperation between good players; update cautiously from observed actions and treat public claims as uncertain evidence.
Cooperate with an untested partner: mutual cooperation benefits both good players, while I’ll update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with untested opponents when good-player welfare is most likely to benefit; update cautiously from observed defections and cooperation.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P2’s action. P4, P5, and P10 cooperated against my defection, so I assess them as good; update remaining beliefs using the count-conditioned prior.

Cooperate with P5: the updated chance they are good makes mutual cooperation yield greater expected good-player welfare than defection. Treat public claims as weak evidence and update from observed actions.
Cooperate with unobserved P9 to support shared welfare if they are good; update private identity beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with unobserved P8: they are more likely good than selfish, and mutual cooperation yields greater total welfare among good players. Treat P2’s defection as some evidence of selfishness; prior cooperation by P5 and P7 favors good.
Cooperate with P1 absent evidence of selfishness to support shared welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt when an opponent appears likely selfish.

Defect in this one-time encounter to maximize my payoff regardless of P4’s action. Treat observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good player and P2’s defection as evidence of selfishness; public claims remain unverified.
Defect to maximize my payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions and treat public claims as unverified.

Cooperate with unobserved P10 to support mutual welfare if they are good; reserve defection for opponents with stronger evidence of selfishness. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions and treat claims as unverified.
Cooperate with an untested partner to maximize expected welfare among good players; update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with an untested opponent when they are likely good, since that maximizes total good-player payoffs; defect against likely selfish opponents. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions and unverified claims.

Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P2’s defection raises my suspicion, though good players may also defect conditionally; cooperation against my past defections is strong evidence of a good role.

Cooperate with P2: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and the remaining selfish-player probability is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P5 absent evidence of selfishness; update identity beliefs from observed actions and favor welfare among good players.
Defect against P6: the reported defection against cooperation is meaningful evidence of selfishness. Cooperations by P5, P7, and P8 favor good; P2’s defection favors selfish.

Cooperate with P3 absent evidence of selfishness to support shared welfare. Update beliefs from observed actions, accounting for the possibility that good players defect when they suspect a selfish opponent.

Defect to maximize my payoff in this encounter regardless of P8’s action. Lower beliefs for players observed cooperating; raise them for observed defections, while treating unverified public claims as uncertain evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff; update beliefs from observed behavior and treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with unobserved P9 to support shared welfare if they are good; defect only when evidence of selfishness is strong. Treat actions and public claims as evidence, not proof.
Cooperate with the untested P2 to support mutual welfare if they are good; update beliefs from observed actions while accounting for uncertainty about identities.

Cooperate with an untested opponent: mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare, and against a good player cooperation is never worse when they defect. Update beliefs cautiously from observed behavior and unverified claims.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P7’s action. P4’s report that P3 and P7 cooperated with them is evidence they are good; retain uncertainty about players whose actions are ambiguous.

Defect against P6 given the leader’s report that P6 defected against cooperation; treat that claim as evidence, not certainty. Update beliefs from observed actions and account for uncertainty in the report.
Cooperate when likely-good players’ shared welfare outweighs the risk of exploitation; update identity beliefs from observed actions and treat public claims as uncertain evidence.
Cooperate with P3: P4 reports that P3 cooperated with them, which favors P3 being good. Cooperating supports shared welfare when both players are good; update from our encounter.

Cooperate with P5, whose selfishness is unconfirmed; mutual cooperation among good players maximizes their shared welfare. Update beliefs from observed behavior while allowing good players may defect against suspected selfish opponents.

Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P6’s action. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of goodness, while allowing for uncertainty and the unknown selfish-player count.
Defect to maximize my payoff; update beliefs from observed behavior and treat public claims as uncertain.

Defect against P2 given reported defection against a cooperative partner; cooperate with unknowns unless evidence suggests selfishness. Treat public encounter claims as useful but unverified evidence.
Cooperate with untested P5 to support mutual welfare if they are good; update identity beliefs from observed actions.

Against P4, defect because I judge selfishness more likely than goodness; otherwise cooperate to maximize good-player welfare. Update beliefs from observed actions, treating public claims as unverified.

Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P4, P5, and P10 cooperated against my defections; P4 reports P3 and P7 cooperated with them. P1 and P2’s defections against P4’s cooperation raise suspicion, but claims remain uncertain.

Cooperate with untested P8: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and the chance P8 is selfish is well below the threshold for defection. Treat reports and observed actions as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with P7 given positive evidence they reciprocate; favor mutual cooperation with likely-good players and defect when exploitation seems likely.

Cooperate with untested P10: they are more likely good than selfish, and cooperation gives greater total welfare when both players are good. P2’s repeated defection and P1/P6’s reported defections favor selfishness; cooperation by P3/P5/P7/P8 favors good.

Cooperate with untested P9: shared welfare favors C when P9 is good, and current evidence leaves that more likely. Update beliefs cautiously; repeated defections raise suspicion, while observed cooperation is evidence of being good.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P7’s action; use observed cooperation and defections as evidence while retaining uncertainty.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action; update beliefs from observed behavior and treat claims as unverified.
Defect against P5 given repeated reports of defection against a cooperative partner; update beliefs from observed behavior while treating public claims as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with the untested P9: mutual cooperation maximizes welfare if they are good, and cooperation is preferable across likely good-player responses. Update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P3, whose reported mutual cooperation is evidence they are likely good; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Treat public claims and observed behavior as evidence, not certainty.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Keep prior suspicions, but treat P4’s reports as uncertain; direct cooperation against my defections is strong evidence of a good role.

Defect against P1 given the leader’s repeated reports of defection against cooperation. Treat reports as fallible; observed cooperation is strong evidence of good intent, and I update beliefs from both direct encounters and credible reports.
Cooperate: if P6 is good, C better supports shared welfare even if they defect; defect only if selfishness is sufficiently likely. Update beliefs from observed actions, treating reports as uncertain.

Cooperate with P4: their consistent welfare-focused messages modestly favor good, and mutual cooperation benefits good players. Reported defections make P1, P2, and P6 more suspect; my own encounters favor P3, P5, P7, and P8.

Cooperate with P2 because shared welfare favors C when P2 is good, which remains more likely. Treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, of selfishness; observed cooperation indicates good status.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P9’s action. Use observed behavior as uncertain evidence about identities and retain uncertainty about the selfish-player count.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action; update beliefs from observed behavior and treat claims as unverified.
Defect against P6 given repeated reports of defection against a cooperative partner; cooperate with known cooperators. Treat reported encounters as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with untested P8: mutual cooperation yields greater welfare when both players are good. Defecting would only help if P8 is selfish; update beliefs from observed behavior.

Defect against P2 given the report that they defected against a cooperating partner; if P2 is selfish, D improves my payoff, while cooperation is better for shared welfare with a good partner. Treat the report as evidence, not certainty.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Direct cooperation against my defections is strong evidence of a good role; defections raise suspicion but may be strategic.
Cooperate with untested P10: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and the available evidence does not make selfishness likely enough to justify defection. Treat public claims as fallible.

Cooperate with P4: mutual cooperation best supports shared welfare if they are good, and their public messages weakly suggest that. Update identity beliefs from observed actions while treating claims as uncertain.

Defect against P1: repeated reports of defection against cooperation make selfishness more likely, and D avoids receiving zero if P1 defects. Keep reports tentative because public claims are unverified.
Cooperate with P7: P4 reports their mutual cooperation, making P7 more likely good; C maximizes shared welfare when both players are good.

Defect in the final encounter; D maximizes my payoff regardless of P9’s action. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of goodness, while retaining uncertainty about identities.
Defect for my payoff; use observed actions and cautious interpretation of public claims to estimate others’ identities.
Cooperate with P4 based on its prior cooperation and consistent stated intent; mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. Treat reported behavior as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with P3, whose earlier cooperation indicates they are good; mutual cooperation maximizes welfare for us both.

Cooperate with P10: their earlier C with me is evidence they may be good, and mutual cooperation benefits good players. Update identity beliefs from observed behavior, treating public claims as unverified.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P2’s action. P2’s defections raise suspicion; cooperation against my defections and P4’s reported observations support low estimates for others.
Cooperate with P8, whose earlier cooperation against my C strongly supports good intent. Treat the leader’s reports as fallible evidence and use direct encounter behavior to update beliefs.
Cooperate with P7, who has reciprocated before; mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. Treat prior defections as evidence, not certainty, about selfishness.

Cooperate with P1: our D-D encounter was inconclusive, and P1 is more likely good than selfish. Prioritize shared welfare among good players; treat the leader’s repeated P1 claims cautiously because they conflict with the rotation.
Cooperate with P5, whose previous cooperation establishes they are good. C maximizes welfare for us both; observed defections by others are evidence, not proof, of selfishness.
